about: Ready-made selections on the Clinic Forms page. Each item is doc:<document id> or layout:<form id> (DEM is the Demographics registration form). Printed in this order. "about" (optional) is one line saying what the packet is for, shown when staff point at its button. A country pack's packets.json adds packets and replaces these by id (the US pack's new-patient packet adds the privacy notice, sliding fee application and nondiscrimination notice).

packets.title: After the visit (summary and work or school note)
packets.about: For the patient to take home: what was found and what to do next, and a note confirming the visit without saying why.

packets.title: Procedure visit (consent, then the visit summary)
packets.about: Consent signed before the procedure starts, then the summary and a work or school note to take home.

packets.title: Yearly adult screen (anxiety, depression and substance use)
packets.about: Every adult, once a year: the short first stage of each screen. A positive answer opens its follow-up: the GAD-7 or PHQ-9 after the PHQ-4, TAPS-2 after TAPS-1.

packets.title: After a positive depression screen (PHQ-9, then the ASQ)
packets.about: For a positive PHQ-4 depression score or PHQ-2. The ASQ follows a positive answer to question 9, or whenever clinic protocol calls for it. A repeat PHQ-9 at follow-up shows remission (CMS159).

packets.title: After a positive anxiety screen (GAD-7)
packets.about: For a positive PHQ-4 anxiety score: the GAD-7 and its severity bands.

packets.title: Relationship safety (HARK), given in private
packets.about: Four questions about a partner or ex-partner in the past year. Give it when the patient is alone, never with a partner present; 1 or more yes is a positive screen.

packets.title: Depression and anxiety screening
packets.about: The PHQ-9 and GAD-7 together, for a visit about mood or anxiety.

packets.title: Quick screening (depression and alcohol)
packets.about: Two short screens, depression and alcohol, when there is time for no more.

packets.title: Behavioral health screening (depression, anxiety, PTSD, substance use)
packets.about: A behavioral health intake: depression, anxiety, PTSD and the four substances TAPS-1 asks about.

packets.title: Substance use (TAPS-1, then TAPS-2 for any substance it finds)
packets.about: For a positive TAPS-1, or a visit about substance use.

packets.title: Positive screen handoff (internal referral and staff handoff)
packets.about: For staff, with a follow-up packet: the warm handoff to behavioral health, care management, nutrition or social work, recorded so the referral can be followed to completion.

packets.title: Starting a controlled medicine (agreement, substance use and depression screens)
packets.about: Before a long-term opioid, sedative or stimulant: the agreement, with TAPS-1 for substance use and the PHQ-9 for depression.

packets.title: Older adult add-on, 65 and over (falls and depression)
packets.about: At 65 and over, with the yearly adult screen: falls risk (Stay Independent) and the Geriatric Depression Scale, which some clinics use for older adults in place of the PHQ.
